note: LeetCode question mapping. Edit freely: concepts/patternTemplate are topic ids, warmups are built-in problem ids. Run `npm run verify:map` after editing.

questions.title: Running Sum of 1D Array
questions.summary: Return an array where each element is the sum of all elements up to that index.
hints: Each output value builds on the previous output value.
result[i] = result[i-1] + nums[i].
One pass, O(1) extra space if you overwrite the input.

questions.title: Longest Common Prefix
questions.summary: Longest prefix shared by all strings in an array.
hints: The answer can never be longer than the shortest string.
Compare column by column across all strings.
Stop at the first column where a character differs or a string ends.

questions.title: Find the Index of the First Occurrence in a String
questions.summary: Index of the first occurrence of one string inside another, or -1.
hints: Try every starting position.
Compare the substring at each start.
O(n·m) is fine here; KMP is the advanced follow-up.

questions.title: Valid Anagram
questions.summary: Are two strings anagrams of each other?
hints: Anagrams have identical letter counts.
Count letters of s up and letters of t down.
With 26 lowercase letters an int array is enough.

questions.title: Contains Duplicate
questions.summary: Does any value appear at least twice?
hints: You need fast "have I seen this?" checks.
A set gives O(1) membership.
Return true the first time an element is already in the set.

questions.title: Majority Element
questions.summary: Find the value that appears more than half the time.
hints: A hash map count works in O(n) space.
For O(1) space, pair off different values.
Boyer–Moore voting: keep a candidate and a counter.

questions.title: First Unique Character in a String
questions.summary: Index of the first character that appears exactly once.
hints: Two passes.
First count every character.
Then return the first index whose count is 1.

questions.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
questions.summary: One buy and one later sell: maximise profit from a price array.
hints: For each day, what is the best day to have bought before it?
Keep the minimum price seen so far.
Profit today = price - min so far; track the max of that.

questions.title: Squares of a Sorted Array
questions.summary: Sorted squares of a sorted array (with negatives) in O(n).
hints: The largest square is at one of the two ends.
Compare absolute values at both ends.
Fill the output from the back with the larger square.

questions.title: Merge Sorted Array
questions.summary: Merge a second sorted array into the first one, which has spare space at the end.
hints: Filling from the front overwrites values you still need.
Fill from the back.
Three pointers: end of nums1 data, end of nums2, write position.

questions.title: Maximum Subarray
questions.summary: Find the contiguous subarray with the largest sum.
hints: At index i, the best subarray ending here either continues or starts fresh.
cur = max(x, cur + x).
Track the best cur seen. Start from nums[0], not 0.

questions.title: Product of Array Except Self
questions.summary: For each index, product of every other element, without division, in O(n).
hints: answer[i] = (product of everything left of i) × (product of everything right of i).
Fill left products in one pass into the output array.
Second pass from the right with a running suffix product.

questions.title: Move Zeroes
questions.summary: Move all zeros to the end in-place, keeping the order of non-zero elements.
hints: Think of a write pointer for the next non-zero position.
Copy every non-zero to nums[write] and advance write.
Fill the rest with zeros (or swap instead of copy).

questions.title: Rotate Array
questions.summary: Shift every element of an array k places to the right, wrapping around, in place.
hints: k can be larger than n.
Reversing the whole array, then the two parts, rotates it.
Reverse all, reverse first k, reverse the rest (k %= n).

questions.title: Find Pivot Index
questions.summary: Leftmost index where the sum to the left equals the sum to the right.
hints: If you know the total sum, can you get the right sum from the left sum?
right = total - left - nums[i].
Scan once updating left; return the first i where left == right.

questions.title: Subarray Sum Equals K
questions.summary: Count contiguous subarrays whose sum is exactly k (negatives allowed).
hints: A sliding window fails because of negatives. What else describes a subarray sum?
sum(i..j) = prefix[j] - prefix[i-1]. You need earlier prefixes equal to prefix - k.
Hash map of prefix-sum counts, seeded with {0: 1}.

questions.title: Range Sum Query - Immutable
questions.summary: Answer many sum(left..right) queries on a fixed array.
hints: Precompute once, answer each query fast.
Prefix sums with a leading 0.
sum(l..r) = pre[r+1] - pre[l].

questions.title: Contiguous Array
questions.summary: Longest subarray with an equal number of 0s and 1s.
hints: Turn 0 into -1; then you want a subarray summing to 0.
Equal prefix sums at two positions mean a zero-sum subarray between them.
Store the first index of each prefix sum.

questions.title: Valid Palindrome
questions.summary: Is the string a palindrome after lowercasing and removing non-alphanumerics?
hints: Compare from both ends inward.
Skip characters that are not letters or digits on each side.
Compare lowercase versions; stop when the pointers cross.

questions.title: Reverse Words in a String
questions.summary: Reverse word order, collapsing extra spaces.
hints: First get a clean list of words.
Splitting on runs of whitespace removes the extra spaces.
Reverse the list and join with single spaces.

questions.title: Valid Palindrome II
questions.summary: Can a string become a palindrome by deleting at most one character?
hints: Two pointers until the first mismatch.
At a mismatch, try skipping the left char or the right char.
Check the remaining part is a palindrome for either choice.

questions.title: String Compression
questions.summary: Compress runs of repeated characters in a char array in place and return the new length.
hints: Use a read pointer and a write pointer.
For each run, write the character, then its count if > 1.
Write multi-digit counts digit by digit.

questions.title: Two Sum
questions.summary: Indices of the two numbers that add up to target.
hints: For each number x, which other number do you need?
Have you already seen target - x? A hash map answers that in O(1).
Check the map before inserting x so it never pairs with itself.

questions.title: Group Anagrams
questions.summary: Group strings that are anagrams of each other.
hints: Anagrams should map to the same key.
Sorted letters (or a 26-count tuple) is a canonical key.
Map key → list of words; return the map values.

questions.title: Ransom Note
questions.summary: Can one string be built using the letters of another (each letter once)?
hints: Count available letters.
Decrement for each letter the note needs.
Any count below zero means impossible.

questions.title: Isomorphic Strings
questions.summary: Can the characters of one string be consistently replaced to get the other?
hints: The mapping must be one-to-one both ways.
Keep two maps: s→t and t→s.
Any conflict in either map means false.

questions.title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
questions.summary: Length of the longest run of consecutive integers, in O(n).
hints: Sorting is O(n log n). Can a set do better?
Only start counting at x when x - 1 is not in the set.
From each start, walk x+1, x+2…. Each number is visited at most twice overall.

questions.title: Subarray Sums Divisible by K
questions.summary: Count subarrays whose sum is a multiple of k.
hints: Two prefix sums with the same remainder mod k.
Count prefix remainders in a map, seeded with {0: 1}.
Normalize negative remainders ((x % k) + k) % k.

questions.title: Valid Sudoku
questions.summary: Check that a partially filled 9×9 board breaks no Sudoku rule.
hints: Each row, column and 3×3 box needs no duplicate digits.
Use sets per row, column and box.
Box index = (r // 3) * 3 + c // 3.

questions.title: Encode and Decode Strings
questions.summary: Design an encoding that turns a list of strings into one string and back.
hints: Any delimiter could appear inside the strings.
Prefix each string with its length.
Format like "len#text"; decode by reading the length first.

questions.title: Two Sum II - Input Array Is Sorted
questions.summary: Sorted array: 1-indexed positions of two numbers summing to target, O(1) space.
hints: The array is sorted. Use that instead of extra memory.
Pointers at both ends: too small → move left, too big → move right.
Return 1-indexed positions.

questions.title: 3Sum
questions.summary: All unique triplets that sum to zero.
hints: Fix one number, then you need a pair summing to its negative.
Sort first, then two pointers for the pair.
Skip equal values for the fixed number and after finding a triplet to avoid duplicates.

questions.title: Container With Most Water
questions.summary: Two lines that hold the most water.
hints: Start with the widest container.
Area is limited by the shorter line.
Move the shorter line inward. Moving the taller one can never help.

questions.title: Trapping Rain Water
questions.summary: Total water trapped between elevation bars.
hints: Water above a bar = min(max left, max right) - height.
Prefix/suffix max arrays give O(n) time and O(n) space.
Two pointers: process the side with the smaller max, it is the binding one.

questions.title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array
questions.summary: Remove duplicates from a sorted array in place and return how many unique values remain.
hints: Duplicates are adjacent.
A write pointer marks where the next unique value goes.
Copy nums[i] only when it differs from the last written value.

questions.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
questions.summary: Length of the longest substring with all distinct characters.
hints: Keep a window that never contains a repeat.
When a repeat enters, move the left edge past its previous position.
Store the last index of each character.

questions.title: Minimum Size Subarray Sum
questions.summary: Shortest subarray (positive numbers) with sum >= target.
hints: All numbers are positive, a window sum only grows when you extend.
Expand right; while sum ≥ target, record length and shrink left.
Return 0 if no window ever reached the target.

questions.title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
questions.summary: Longest window that becomes one repeated letter after at most k replacements.
hints: What makes a window fixable with ≤ k changes?
window length - count of its most frequent letter ≤ k.
Keep counts per letter; the max frequency never needs to decrease for the answer.

questions.title: Maximum Average Subarray I
questions.summary: Maximum average of any contiguous subarray of length k.
hints: Fixed window size.
Slide: add the new element, subtract the one leaving.
Max sum / k is the max average.

questions.title: Fibonacci Number
hints: Write it recursively from the definition first.
Plain recursion recomputes the same values. Memoize.
Or iterate keeping only the last two values.

questions.title: Reverse String
questions.summary: Reverse a character array in place.
hints: Swap from both ends.
Recursively: swap ends, then reverse the middle.
Stop when the pointers meet.

questions.title: Power of Two
questions.summary: Is the given integer a power of two?
hints: Recursively divide by 2 while even.
A power of two has exactly one set bit.

questions.title: Permutation in String
questions.summary: Does s2 contain some permutation of s1 as a substring?
hints: A permutation has the same letter counts.
Slide a window of length len(s1) over s2.
Compare 26-letter count arrays, updating one in and one out per step.

questions.title: Pow(x, n)
questions.summary: Compute x^n in O(log n) using fast exponentiation.
hints: Handle odd n with one extra multiplication.
For negative n use 1/x and -n (beware -2^31 overflow in Java).

questions.title: Fruit Into Baskets
questions.summary: Longest contiguous run containing at most two distinct values.
hints: Variable sliding window.
Count values in the window.
Shrink from the left while there are more than two distinct values.

questions.title: Max Consecutive Ones III
questions.summary: Longest run of 1s if you may flip at most k zeros.
hints: Flip budget = number of zeros allowed in the window.
Expand right; count zeros.
Shrink left while zeros > k.

questions.title: K-th Symbol in Grammar
questions.summary: The k-th symbol in row n of a grammar where 0→01 and 1→10.
hints: Row n is built from row n - 1.
Symbol k in row n comes from symbol ceil(k/2) in row n - 1.
It equals the parent if k is odd, the flipped parent if even.

questions.title: Sort an Array
questions.summary: Sort without the built-in sort: implement merge sort.
hints: You need O(n log n) without the library sort.
Merge sort: sort halves, merge with two pointers.
Use one temp buffer to avoid allocating per call.

questions.title: Sort Colors
questions.summary: Dutch national flag: sort 0s, 1s and 2s in one pass, in place.
hints: Only three values. Can you place them in one pass?
Keep low (next 0 slot), mid (scanner), high (next 2 slot).
Swap 0s to low, 2s to high; do not advance mid after swapping with high.

questions.title: Largest Number
questions.summary: Arrange non-negative integers to form the largest possible number string.
hints: Normal numeric sorting is wrong (9 should come before 34).
Compare a+b vs b+a as strings.
Sort with that comparator; handle all-zero input.

questions.title: Merge Intervals
questions.summary: Merge all overlapping intervals.
hints: Overlaps are easy to see once intervals are ordered.
Sort by start.
If the next start ≤ last end, extend the last end; otherwise append.

questions.title: Sort Characters By Frequency
questions.summary: Reorder a string so more frequent characters come first.
hints: Count characters.
Sort characters by count (or bucket by count).
Build the output with each char repeated count times.

questions.title: Insert Interval
questions.summary: Insert a new interval into sorted non-overlapping intervals, merging as needed.
hints: Three phases: before, overlapping, after.
Add all intervals ending before the new one starts.
Merge overlapping ones into the new interval, then add the rest.

questions.title: Meeting Rooms
questions.summary: Can one person attend every meeting?
hints: Sort by start.
Check adjacent meetings.
Overlap if a start is before the previous end.

questions.title: Binary Search
questions.summary: Index of target in a sorted array, or -1.
hints: Halve the search space each step.
Compare target with the middle element.
Keep a consistent [lo, hi] convention to avoid off-by-one loops.

questions.title: Search Insert Position
questions.summary: Index of target, or where it would be inserted to keep order.
hints: This is "first index with value ≥ target".
Lower-bound binary search.
If target is larger than everything, the answer is n.

questions.title: Find First and Last Position of Element in Sorted Array
questions.summary: Range [first, last] of target in a sorted array with duplicates.
hints: Two binary searches, not one.
First position = lower bound of target.
Last position = lower bound of target + 1, minus one.

questions.title: Sqrt(x)
questions.summary: Integer square root without library functions.
hints: The answer is the largest m with m*m ≤ x.
Binary search m in [0, x].
Watch overflow of m*m in Java (use long).

questions.title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
questions.summary: Find target in a rotated sorted array in O(log n).
hints: At any mid, one half is sorted.
Check whether target lies inside the sorted half.
If yes search there, otherwise search the other half.

questions.title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
questions.summary: Minimum of a rotated sorted array in O(log n).
hints: Compare mid with the right end.
If nums[mid] > nums[hi], the minimum is right of mid.
Otherwise it is at mid or left of it: hi = mid.

questions.title: Search a 2D Matrix
questions.summary: Search a value in a matrix whose rows are sorted and continue each other.
hints: Read row by row, the matrix is one sorted list.
Binary search over indices 0..m*n-1.
Index i maps to row i / n, column i % n.

questions.title: Find Peak Element
questions.summary: Find any index whose value is larger than its neighbours.
hints: Compare mid with mid + 1.
If the slope goes up, a peak is to the right.
Binary search on the slope direction.

questions.title: Koko Eating Bananas
questions.summary: Minimum eating speed to finish all piles within h hours.
hints: If speed k works, any faster speed works too.
Binary search on the speed between 1 and max(piles).
Hours for speed k = sum of ceil(p / k).

questions.title: Capacity To Ship Packages Within D Days
questions.summary: Smallest ship capacity that ships all packages in order within d days.
hints: If capacity C works, bigger works too.
Binary search C between max(weight) and sum(weights).
Greedy check: fill each day until the next package would overflow.

questions.title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
questions.summary: Median of two sorted arrays in logarithmic time.
hints: Partition both arrays so the left halves together hold half the elements.
Binary search the cut in the shorter array.
Valid when maxLeftA ≤ minRightB and maxLeftB ≤ minRightA.

questions.title: Time Based Key-Value Store
questions.summary: Key-value store returning the latest value at or before a given timestamp.
hints: Timestamps per key arrive increasing.
Store (timestamp, value) lists per key.
Binary search for the last timestamp ≤ query.

questions.title: Reverse Linked List
questions.summary: Reverse a singly linked list.
hints: Flip one arrow at a time.
You need prev, cur and a saved next.
When cur is null, prev is the new head.

questions.title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
questions.summary: Splice two sorted lists into one sorted list.
hints: Repeatedly take the smaller head.
A dummy node avoids special-casing the first node.
Attach whatever list remains at the end.

questions.title: Middle of the Linked List
questions.summary: Return the middle node (second middle if even length).
hints: Two pointers moving at different speeds.
Slow moves 1, fast moves 2.
When fast reaches the end, slow is at the (second) middle.

questions.title: Linked List Cycle
questions.summary: Does a linked list contain a cycle?
hints: A visited set works with O(n) memory.
For O(1), move two pointers at different speeds.
If they ever meet, there is a cycle.

questions.title: Remove Nth Node From End of List
questions.summary: Delete the n-th node from the end in one pass.
hints: Create a gap of n nodes between two pointers.
Use a dummy head so removing the first node is not special.
Move both until fast hits the end; slow.next is the node to remove.

questions.title: Palindrome Linked List
questions.summary: Does a singly linked list read the same forwards and backwards?
hints: Find the middle.
Reverse the second half.
Compare both halves node by node.

questions.title: Reorder List
questions.summary: Reorder L0→Ln→L1→Ln-1… in place.
hints: This combines three simpler list operations.
Find the middle, reverse the second half.
Merge the two halves alternately.

questions.title: Linked List Cycle II
questions.summary: Return the node where a linked list cycle begins.
hints: First detect the cycle with fast/slow pointers.
After they meet, reset one pointer to head.
Move both one step at a time; they meet at the cycle start.

questions.title: Add Two Numbers
questions.summary: Add two numbers stored as reversed digit lists.
hints: Add digit by digit like on paper.
Digits are already least-significant first.
Carry forward; keep going while either list or the carry remains.

questions.title: LRU Cache
questions.summary: get/put in O(1) with least-recently-used eviction.
hints: You need O(1) lookup and O(1) "move to most recent".
Hash map + doubly linked list.
On get/put move the node to the front; evict from the back.

questions.title: Copy List with Random Pointer
questions.summary: Deep-copy a linked list whose nodes also have a random pointer.
hints: You need to find the copy of any original node.
Map original node → copy.
Two passes: create copies, then wire next and random.

questions.title: Valid Parentheses
questions.summary: Are the brackets ()[]{} balanced and properly nested?
hints: The most recent unmatched opener must close first.
Use a stack of openers.
On a closer, the top must be its partner; at the end the stack must be empty.

questions.title: Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation
questions.summary: Evaluate a postfix expression (+ - * /, truncating division).
hints: Operands wait until their operator arrives.
Push numbers; on an operator pop two and push the result.
Order matters for - and /; division truncates toward zero.

questions.title: Min Stack
questions.summary: Stack supporting push, pop, top and getMin in O(1).
hints: The minimum changes as you push and pop.
Store the minimum-so-far alongside each element.
getMin reads the top pair's minimum.

questions.title: Implement Queue using Stacks
questions.summary: Build a FIFO queue using only stack operations.
hints: One stack for input, one for output.
Move items to the output stack only when it is empty.
Each element moves once → amortized O(1).

questions.title: Asteroid Collision
questions.summary: Simulate moving asteroids that explode on collision and report the survivors.
hints: Only a right-moving asteroid followed by a left-moving one collide.
Keep survivors on a stack.
For each left-mover, pop smaller right-movers; resolve ties.

questions.title: Decode String
questions.summary: Expand an encoded string like 3[a2[c]].
hints: Brackets nest. The innermost finishes first.
On "[", push the current string and repeat count.
On "]", pop and append the current string repeated.

questions.title: Basic Calculator II
questions.summary: Evaluate an expression with + - * / and no parentheses.
hints: * and / bind tighter than + and -.
Keep a stack of terms; apply * and / to the top immediately.
Sum the stack at the end (division truncates toward zero).

questions.title: Daily Temperatures
questions.summary: For each day, how many days until a warmer temperature?

python: list as a stack of indices

hints: Each day waits for the next warmer day.
Keep a stack of indices still waiting (decreasing temps).
When a warmer day arrives, pop and set answer = i - j.

questions.title: Next Greater Element II
questions.summary: Next greater element in a circular array.

python: list as a stack of indices

hints: Same as next greater element, but the array wraps.
Iterate 2n times using i % n.
Only push indices during the first pass.

questions.title: Online Stock Span
questions.summary: For each new price, how many consecutive days (including today) had price ≤ today?

python: list as a stack of indices

hints: Previous smaller days can be merged.
Stack of (price, span), decreasing prices.
Pop while top price ≤ today, adding their spans.

questions.title: Next Greater Element I
questions.summary: For each value of one array, the next greater element in a second array.

python: list as a stack of indices

hints: Precompute next greater for every value of nums2.
Monotonic decreasing stack over nums2.
Store answers in a map; look up nums1 values.

questions.title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
questions.summary: Area of the largest rectangle in a histogram.

python: list as a stack of indices

hints: For each bar, how far can it extend left and right?
The boundaries are the nearest smaller bars on each side.
An increasing stack finds both: when a bar is popped, its width is known.

questions.title: Remove K Digits
questions.summary: Smallest number after removing k digits.

python: list as a stack of indices

hints: A larger digit before a smaller one should go.
Increasing monotonic stack of digits.
Pop while the top is larger and k > 0; strip leading zeros.

questions.title: Car Fleet
questions.summary: How many groups of cars arrive at a target when faster cars cannot pass slower ones?

python: list as a stack of indices

hints: Compute each car's arrival time.
Process cars from closest to the target.
A car that would arrive no later than the fleet ahead joins it.

questions.title: Sliding Window Maximum
questions.summary: Max of every window of size k in O(n).
hints: A heap works but can be O(n log n).
Keep a deque of indices with decreasing values.
Pop from the back when smaller, from the front when out of the window.

questions.title: Number of Recent Calls
questions.summary: Count requests within the last 3000 ms.
hints: Requests arrive in increasing time order.
A queue of timestamps.
Pop from the front while older than t - 3000; return the size.

questions.title: Design Circular Queue
questions.summary: Implement a fixed-size circular queue.
hints: Use an array and wrap indices with modulo.
Track head index and current size.
Tail = (head + size) % capacity.

questions.title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
questions.summary: Number of nodes on the longest root-to-leaf path.

java: a field for a global answer

hints: Depth of a tree depends on its subtrees' depths.
1 + max(depth(left), depth(right)).
An empty tree has depth 0.

questions.title: Invert Binary Tree
questions.summary: Mirror a binary tree.

java: a field for a global answer

hints: Do the same thing at every node.
Swap left and right children.
Recurse into both subtrees (pre or post order both work).

questions.title: Same Tree
questions.summary: Are two binary trees structurally identical with equal values?

java: a field for a global answer

hints: Compare structure and values together.
Both null → same; one null → different.
Values equal and both subtrees same.

questions.title: Binary Tree Inorder Traversal
questions.summary: Return a binary tree's in-order traversal.

java: a field for a global answer

hints: Left, node, right.
Recursive is three lines.
Iterative: push left spine onto a stack, pop, go right.

questions.title: Diameter of Binary Tree
questions.summary: Longest path (in edges) between any two nodes.

java: a field for a global answer

hints: The longest path passes through some highest node.
At each node, path length = left height + right height.
Return height to the parent; keep the best path in an outer variable.

questions.title: Balanced Binary Tree
questions.summary: Is every node's left and right height within one of each other?

java: a field for a global answer

hints: You need heights of subtrees.
Compute height bottom-up.
Return a sentinel (like -1) as soon as a subtree is unbalanced.

questions.title: Subtree of Another Tree
questions.summary: Does one tree appear as a subtree of another?

java: a field for a global answer

hints: Reuse "same tree".
Check sameTree at every node of the big tree.
Recurse left and right if the current node does not match.

questions.title: Path Sum
questions.summary: Is there a root-to-leaf path with a given sum?

java: a field for a global answer

hints: Subtract each node's value as you go down.
Check at leaves only.
Leaf with remaining sum 0 → true.

questions.title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
questions.summary: Values level by level, left to right.
hints: Visit nodes level by level.
BFS with a queue.
Process exactly len(queue) nodes per level.

questions.title: Binary Tree Right Side View
questions.summary: Values visible from the right, top to bottom.
hints: Which node is visible on each level?
BFS by level: take the last node of each level.
Or DFS right-first and record the first node at each new depth.

questions.title: Binary Tree Zigzag Level Order Traversal
questions.summary: Level order traversal alternating left-to-right and right-to-left.
hints: Plain BFS by levels.
Reverse every other level.
Or use a deque and append to the front on odd levels.

questions.title: Count Good Nodes in Binary Tree
questions.summary: Count nodes that are at least as large as every node on the path from the root.

java: a field for a global answer

hints: Carry information down the path.
Pass the maximum seen so far.
Count the node if its value ≥ that maximum.

questions.title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree
questions.summary: Lowest common ancestor of two nodes in a general binary tree.

java: a field for a global answer

hints: No ordering to guide you. Search both sides.
Return the node if it is p or q.
If both sides return non-null, the current node is the LCA.

questions.title: Construct Binary Tree from Preorder and Inorder Traversal
questions.summary: Rebuild a tree from its preorder and inorder traversals.

java: a field for a global answer

hints: Preorder's first element is the root.
Its position in inorder splits left and right subtrees.
Use a value→index map and recurse with index ranges.

questions.title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
questions.summary: Maximum sum of any path between two nodes in a binary tree.

java: a field for a global answer

hints: A path bends at one top node.
At each node, best = val + max(0, leftGain) + max(0, rightGain).
Return val + max(leftGain, rightGain, 0) upward.

questions.title: Serialize and Deserialize Binary Tree
questions.summary: Convert a binary tree to a string and back.
hints: Include null markers so the shape is recoverable.
Preorder with "#" for null.
Deserialize by consuming tokens recursively in the same order.

questions.title: Validate Binary Search Tree
questions.summary: Is this binary tree a valid BST (strict)?
hints: Checking only parent vs child is not enough.
Every node must lie inside a (low, high) range from its ancestors.
Pass the range down; or check in-order traversal is strictly increasing.

questions.title: Kth Smallest Element in a BST
questions.summary: k-th smallest value (1-indexed) in a BST.
hints: Which traversal of a BST is sorted?
In-order traversal visits values in increasing order.
Stop at the k-th visited node (iterative stack makes this easy).

questions.title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Search Tree
questions.summary: LCA value of two nodes in a BST.
hints: Use the BST ordering to decide where to go.
If both values are smaller, go left; both larger, go right.
The first node where they split is the answer.

questions.title: Search in a Binary Search Tree
questions.summary: Find the node with a given value in a BST.
hints: Compare and go one way.
Smaller → left, larger → right.
Return null when you fall off the tree.

questions.title: Insert into a Binary Search Tree
questions.summary: Insert a value into a BST.
hints: Walk down like a search.
Stop at the null child where it belongs.
Attach a new node there.

questions.title: Kth Largest Element in an Array
questions.summary: k-th largest element without fully sorting.
hints: You do not need everything sorted.
Keep a min-heap of the k largest so far.
Its top is the answer. (Quickselect is the O(n) average follow-up.)

questions.title: Last Stone Weight
questions.summary: Repeatedly smash the two heaviest stones.
hints: You repeatedly need the two largest.
A max-heap.
Push back the difference when stones differ.

questions.title: K Closest Points to Origin
questions.summary: k points nearest to (0,0), any order.
hints: Compare squared distances; no sqrt needed.
Keep a max-heap of size k by distance.
Pop when size exceeds k.

questions.title: Kth Largest Element in a Stream
questions.summary: Keep returning the k-th largest value as numbers are added.
hints: You only care about the k largest values.
Min-heap of size k.
Its top is the k-th largest.

questions.title: Merge k Sorted Lists
questions.summary: Merge k sorted linked lists into one.
hints: You always need the smallest current head among k lists.
A min-heap of heads gives that in O(log k).
Pop smallest, append it, push its next.

questions.title: Top K Frequent Elements
questions.summary: The k most frequent values (any order).
hints: First count frequencies.
Then keep the k most frequent with a size-k heap.
Bucket sort by frequency gives O(n).

questions.title: Find Median from Data Stream
questions.summary: addNum / findMedian with two heaps.
hints: Split numbers into a lower and an upper half.
Max-heap for the lower half, min-heap for the upper half.
Rebalance so sizes differ by at most one; median comes from the tops.

questions.title: Task Scheduler
questions.summary: Minimum time slots to run tasks when equal tasks need a cooldown between them.
hints: The most frequent task decides the frame.
Frames: (maxCount - 1) × (n + 1) + number of tasks with maxCount.
Answer is the max of that and the total number of tasks.

questions.title: Reorganize String
questions.summary: Rearrange a string so no two adjacent characters are equal.
hints: Impossible if a character appears more than (n + 1) / 2 times.
Greedily place the most frequent remaining character.
Max-heap of counts; hold back the last used character for one step.

questions.title: Flood Fill
questions.summary: Recolor the connected region containing (sr, sc).
hints: Recolor everything connected to the start with the same color.
DFS/BFS over 4 neighbours.
If the new color equals the old one, return immediately (else infinite loop).

questions.title: Number of Islands
questions.summary: Count 4-directionally connected groups of land.
hints: Each island is one connected component.
Scan the grid; when you find land, count it and flood it.
Mark visited cells (e.g. set to water) so they are not counted again.

questions.title: Max Area of Island
questions.summary: Largest island area in a grid.
hints: Same as counting islands.
DFS returns the size of what it floods.
Track the max size.

questions.title: Find if Path Exists in Graph
questions.summary: Is there a path between two nodes of an undirected graph?
hints: Build an adjacency list.
BFS or DFS from source.
Or Union-Find and compare roots.

questions.title: Clone Graph
questions.summary: Deep-copy an undirected graph.
hints: Visited nodes must map to their copies.
Map original → clone.
BFS/DFS: create clones on first sight, then link neighbours.

questions.title: Pacific Atlantic Water Flow
questions.summary: Cells from which water can flow to both oceans.
hints: Searching from every cell is slow.
Reverse it: flow uphill from each ocean's border.
Answer = cells reached from both searches.

questions.title: Surrounded Regions
questions.summary: Capture regions of O cells that are fully surrounded by X.
hints: Which O cells can never be captured?
Those connected to the border.
Mark border-connected Os first, flip the rest, restore the marks.

questions.title: Number of Enclaves
questions.summary: Count land cells that cannot walk off the grid edge.
hints: Which land can reach the border?
Flood from every border land cell.
Count land cells left unvisited.

questions.title: Rotting Oranges
questions.summary: Minutes until all oranges rot (multi-source BFS), or -1.
hints: All rotten oranges spread at the same time.
Multi-source BFS starting with every rotten orange.
Count BFS levels; check for leftover fresh oranges at the end.

questions.title: Shortest Path in Binary Matrix
questions.summary: Shortest 8-directional clear path from top-left to bottom-right.
hints: Unweighted shortest path → BFS.
Neighbors are all 8 directions.
Check start and end cells are 0; count cells, not moves.

questions.title: 01 Matrix
questions.summary: Distance from each cell to the nearest 0.
hints: Starting a BFS from every cell is too slow.
Start one BFS from all zeros at once.
Each cell's distance is set the first time BFS reaches it.

questions.title: Word Ladder
questions.summary: Shortest transformation sequence length between two words changing one letter at a time.
hints: Words are nodes; one-letter changes are edges.
BFS from the begin word.
Generate neighbours by trying all 26 letters at each position.

questions.title: Course Schedule
questions.summary: Can all courses be finished given prerequisites (cycle detection)?
hints: This is a directed graph. When is finishing impossible?
A cycle makes it impossible.
Kahn's algorithm: if you can process all nodes by in-degree 0, no cycle.

questions.title: Course Schedule II
questions.summary: Return a valid order to take all courses, or an empty list.
hints: Same graph as Course Schedule.
Kahn's algorithm produces the order directly.
If fewer than n courses are output, there is a cycle.

questions.title: Find Eventual Safe States
questions.summary: Nodes from which every path ends at a terminal node.
hints: Nodes on or leading into cycles are unsafe.
Reverse the edges and run Kahn from terminal nodes.
Or DFS with three colors (unvisited, visiting, safe).

questions.title: Alien Dictionary
questions.summary: Derive a letter order from words sorted in an unknown alphabet.
hints: Compare adjacent words.
The first differing letters give one ordering edge.
Topological sort; watch for prefix-invalid input and cycles.

questions.title: Network Delay Time
questions.summary: Time for a signal from k to reach all nodes (Dijkstra).
hints: Weighted shortest paths from one source.
Dijkstra with a min-heap.
Answer = max distance, or -1 if some node is unreachable.

questions.title: Path With Minimum Effort
questions.summary: Route across a grid minimizing the largest height difference along the path.
hints: Path cost is the max step, not the sum.
Dijkstra where distance = max effort so far.
Or binary search the effort with BFS.

questions.title: Cheapest Flights Within K Stops
questions.summary: Cheapest flight price from source to destination with at most k stops.
hints: Plain Dijkstra ignores the stop limit.
Bellman–Ford with k + 1 rounds.
Relax from a copy of the previous round's prices.

questions.title: Swim in Rising Water
questions.summary: Earliest time you can swim from top-left to bottom-right as water rises.
hints: Time needed = max elevation on the path.
Dijkstra with a min-heap on max-so-far.
Or binary search the time with BFS.

questions.title: Number of Provinces
questions.summary: Count connected components from an adjacency matrix.
hints: Count connected components.
DFS from each unvisited city, or Union-Find.
The matrix is the adjacency matrix.

questions.title: Redundant Connection
questions.summary: The edge whose removal turns the graph back into a tree.
hints: Which edge first connects two already-connected nodes?
Union-Find while adding edges in order.
The edge whose endpoints share a root is the answer.

questions.title: Min Cost to Connect All Points
questions.summary: Minimum total Manhattan distance to connect all points.
hints: This is a minimum spanning tree.
Prim's with a min-heap, or Kruskal with Union-Find.
With dense graphs, O(n²) Prim without a heap is fine.

questions.title: Accounts Merge
questions.summary: Merge accounts that share any email.
hints: Emails are nodes; accounts link emails.
Union all emails within each account.
Group emails by root, sort, attach the name.

questions.title: Number of Connected Components in an Undirected Graph
questions.summary: Count connected components in an undirected graph.
hints: Start with n components.
Each successful union reduces the count by one.
Or count DFS starts over unvisited nodes.

questions.title: Jump Game
questions.summary: Can you reach the last index given max jump lengths?
hints: Track how far you can possibly reach.
If i is beyond the farthest reach, you are stuck.
farthest = max(farthest, i + nums[i]).

questions.title: Jump Game II
questions.summary: Minimum jumps to reach the last index.
hints: Think in levels like BFS: all indices reachable with k jumps.
Track the end of the current level and the farthest next reach.
When i reaches the current end, jump++ and extend to farthest.

questions.title: Gas Station
questions.summary: Starting station to complete a circular route, or -1.
hints: If total gas < total cost, it is impossible.
If the tank goes negative at i, no start between the old start and i works.
Restart from i + 1 with an empty tank.

questions.title: Assign Cookies
questions.summary: Maximize children satisfied when each child needs a cookie of at least some size.
hints: Small cookies should go to the least greedy children.
Sort both lists.
Two pointers: give the current cookie to the current child if it fits.

questions.title: Non-overlapping Intervals
questions.summary: Minimum intervals to remove so the rest do not overlap.
hints: Maximize how many you keep instead.
Keep the interval that ends earliest.
Sort by end; count intervals starting at or after the last kept end.

questions.title: Meeting Rooms II
questions.summary: Minimum number of rooms so that no two overlapping meetings share one.
hints: Count how many meetings are active at once.
Sort by start; keep a min-heap of end times.
Before adding a meeting, free rooms whose end ≤ its start.

questions.title: Minimum Number of Arrows to Burst Balloons
questions.summary: Fewest vertical arrows to burst all horizontal balloons.
hints: Shoot as far right as possible while still hitting the current balloon.
Sort by end.
New arrow only when a balloon starts after the last arrow position.

questions.title: Partition Labels
questions.summary: Split a string into as many parts as possible with each letter in only one part.
hints: A part must extend to the last occurrence of every letter in it.
Record each letter's last index.
Extend the current end; cut when i reaches it.

questions.title: Hand of Straights
questions.summary: Can cards be split into groups of consecutive values of a given size?
hints: The smallest card must start a group.
Count cards; process values in sorted order.
For each start, consume one of each of the next groupSize values.

questions.title: Climbing Stairs
questions.summary: Ways to climb n stairs taking 1 or 2 steps.
hints: How can you arrive at step n?
From n-1 or n-2.
ways(n) = ways(n-1) + ways(n-2), Fibonacci with two variables.

questions.title: House Robber
questions.summary: Max sum of non-adjacent elements.
hints: At each house: rob it or skip it.
Rob i → you cannot have robbed i-1.
dp[i] = max(dp[i-1], dp[i-2] + nums[i]).

questions.title: Min Cost Climbing Stairs
questions.summary: Minimum cost to reach the top when each step has a cost and you climb 1 or 2.
hints: Like Climbing Stairs, but minimizing.
dp[i] = cost[i] + min(dp[i-1], dp[i-2]).
Answer = min of the last two.

questions.title: Coin Change
questions.summary: Fewest coins to make an amount (unlimited coins).
hints: Greedy (largest coin first) fails. Try small amounts first.
dp[a] = fewest coins for amount a.
dp[a] = 1 + min(dp[a - c]) over coins; unreachable stays infinity.

questions.title: Decode Ways
questions.summary: Number of ways to decode a digit string with A=1..Z=26.
hints: At each position take one digit or two digits.
A single 0 cannot be decoded alone.
dp[i] = dp[i-1] (if valid 1-digit) + dp[i-2] (if valid 10..26).

questions.title: House Robber II
questions.summary: House Robber where the houses form a circle.
hints: The first and last house cannot both be robbed.
Run House Robber on houses[0..n-2] and houses[1..n-1].
Take the max; handle n == 1.

questions.title: Palindromic Substrings
questions.summary: Count palindromic substrings.
hints: Every palindrome has a center.
Expand around 2n - 1 centers.
Each successful expansion is one more palindrome.

questions.title: Word Break
questions.summary: Can the string be split into dictionary words?
hints: Can the prefix s[:i] be segmented?
dp[i] is true if some dp[j] is true and s[j:i] is a word.
Use a set for the dictionary; dp[0] = true.

questions.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock with Cooldown
questions.summary: Max profit with unlimited trades but a one-day cooldown after selling.
hints: Model the day as states.
States: holding, just sold, resting.
Write each state's transition from yesterday's states.

questions.title: Maximum Subarray Sum with One Deletion
questions.summary: Max subarray sum when you may delete at most one element.
hints: Two Kadane states.
noDel = best ending here without deletion; oneDel = with one deletion.
oneDel = max(oneDel + x, noDel_prev) (deleting x).

questions.title: Unique Paths
questions.summary: Paths from top-left to bottom-right moving only right/down.
hints: You reach a cell only from above or from the left.
First row and column are all 1. One row of memory is enough.

questions.title: Minimum Path Sum
questions.summary: Cheapest top-left to bottom-right path moving right/down.
hints: Same movement as Unique Paths, but minimizing cost.
dp[r][c] = grid[r][c] + min(top, left).
Handle the first row and column separately.

questions.title: Maximal Square
questions.summary: Area of the largest square of 1s in a binary matrix.
hints: dp[r][c] = side of the largest square ending at (r, c).
1 + min(top, left, top-left) when the cell is 1.
Answer = max side squared.

questions.title: Unique Paths II
questions.summary: Unique Paths with blocked cells.
hints: Same recurrence as Unique Paths.
Obstacle cells have 0 ways.
Careful with the first row/column after an obstacle.

questions.title: Longest Common Subsequence
questions.summary: Length of the LCS of two strings.
hints: Compare the last characters of two prefixes.
Equal → 1 + dp[i-1][j-1].
Otherwise max(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1]).

questions.title: Edit Distance
questions.summary: Minimum insert/delete/replace operations to turn word1 into word2.
hints: Think about the last characters of both prefixes.
Equal → no cost; else 1 + min(insert, delete, replace) neighbours.
Base cases: dp[i][0] = i, dp[0][j] = j.

questions.title: Longest Palindromic Subsequence
questions.summary: Length of the longest palindromic subsequence.
hints: Interval DP over s[i..j].
Ends equal → 2 + inner; else max of dropping one end.
Or LCS of s and reverse(s).

questions.title: Interleaving String
questions.summary: Is s3 formed by interleaving s1 and s2 in order?
hints: State: how much of s1 and s2 you have used.
dp[i][j] = s3[:i+j] formable from s1[:i] and s2[:j].
Extend from dp[i-1][j] or dp[i][j-1] when the next char matches.

questions.title: Partition Equal Subset Sum
questions.summary: Can the array be split into two equal-sum subsets?
hints: Equal halves means a subset sums to total / 2.
Odd total → impossible.
0/1 knapsack over reachable sums; iterate sums backwards.

questions.title: Target Sum
questions.summary: Ways to assign +/- signs to reach a target.
hints: Each number gets + or −.
Count ways with a map of reachable sums → counts.
Or transform: subset with sum (total + target) / 2.

questions.title: Coin Change II
questions.summary: Number of coin combinations that make an amount (unlimited coins).
hints: Combinations, not permutations.
Loop coins outside, amounts inside.
dp[a] += dp[a - coin], dp[0] = 1.

questions.title: Last Stone Weight II
questions.summary: Smallest possible weight left after smashing stones in any order.
hints: Smashing assigns + or − to each stone.
You want two groups with sums as close as possible.
Subset-sum DP up to total / 2.

questions.title: Ones and Zeroes
questions.summary: Largest subset of binary strings using at most m zeros and n ones.
hints: Knapsack with two capacities.
dp[z][o] = max strings using z zeros and o ones.
Iterate both capacities backwards for each string.

questions.title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
questions.summary: Length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.
hints: dp[i] = LIS ending exactly at i.
dp[i] = 1 + max(dp[j]) for j < i with nums[j] < nums[i].
O(n log n): keep the smallest tail per length and binary search.

questions.title: Russian Doll Envelopes
questions.summary: Maximum number of envelopes you can nest inside each other.
hints: Sort to reduce to one dimension.
Sort by width ascending, height descending for equal widths.
LIS on heights with binary search.

questions.title: Longest Increasing Path in a Matrix
questions.summary: Longest strictly increasing path in a grid moving in 4 directions.
hints: Paths are increasing, so there are no cycles.
DFS from each cell with memoization.
memo[r][c] = 1 + max over larger neighbours.

questions.title: Subsets
questions.summary: All subsets of distinct numbers.
hints: Every element is either in or out.
Backtrack with a start index.
Record a copy of the current path at every node of the recursion.

questions.title: Permutations
questions.summary: All orderings of distinct numbers.
hints: Choose each unused element for the next position.
Track used elements.
Record when the path has n elements; undo after recursing.

questions.title: Subsets II
questions.summary: All subsets of an array that may contain duplicates, without duplicate subsets.
hints: Duplicates cause repeated branches.
Sort first.
At the same depth, skip nums[i] if it equals nums[i-1] (i > start).

questions.title: Letter Combinations of a Phone Number
questions.summary: All letter strings a phone-digit string could represent.
hints: One digit per recursion level.
Loop over that digit's letters.
Record when the path length equals the digits length.

questions.title: Combination Sum
questions.summary: Unique combinations (reuse allowed) summing to target.
hints: Elements can be reused, order does not matter.
Recurse with the same start index to allow reuse.
Stop when the remaining target is 0 or negative.

questions.title: Generate Parentheses
questions.summary: All well-formed combinations of n pairs of parentheses.
hints: Build the string one character at a time.
You can add "(" while open < n.
You can add ")" only while close < open.

questions.title: Combination Sum II
questions.summary: Unique combinations summing to target, each number used once, input has duplicates.
hints: Like Combination Sum, but no reuse.
Recurse with i + 1.
Sort and skip equal values at the same depth.

questions.title: Palindrome Partitioning
questions.summary: All ways to split a string into palindromic pieces.
hints: Choose the first piece, then partition the rest.
Only cut at palindromic prefixes.
Precompute palindrome table to speed up checks.

questions.title: Word Search
questions.summary: Does the word exist as a path of adjacent cells?
hints: Try starting the word at every cell.
DFS to neighbours matching the next letter.
Mark the cell as used during the path and unmark when backtracking.

questions.title: N-Queens II
questions.summary: Number of ways to place n non-attacking queens.
hints: Place one queen per row.
Track used columns and both diagonals (r - c and r + c).
Count placements that reach row n.

questions.title: N-Queens
questions.summary: List every valid placement of n non-attacking queens.
hints: One queen per row.
Track columns and both diagonals.
Build board strings when a full placement is found.

questions.title: Word Break II
questions.summary: All sentences formed by splitting a string into dictionary words.
hints: Same choices as Word Break, but collect results.
Backtrack over prefixes that are words.
Memoize results per start index.

questions.title: Implement Trie (Prefix Tree)
questions.summary: insert / search / startsWith on a prefix tree.
hints: One node per character, children by letter.
Each node needs an end-of-word flag.
search checks the flag; startsWith only checks the path exists.

questions.title: Design Add and Search Words Data Structure
questions.summary: Trie where search supports '.' wildcards.
hints: Build on a trie.
'.' means try every child.
DFS through the trie with the word index.

questions.title: Word Search II
questions.summary: Find all dictionary words that can be traced in a letter grid.
hints: Searching each word separately repeats work.
Put the words in a trie.
DFS the grid while walking the trie; prune dead branches.

questions.title: Replace Words
questions.summary: Replace each word in a sentence with its shortest dictionary root.
hints: You need prefix lookups.
Insert roots into a trie.
For each word, walk the trie and stop at the first end-of-word.

questions.title: Single Number
questions.summary: Every element appears twice except one; find it in O(1) space.
hints: Pairs should cancel out.
a ^ a = 0 and a ^ 0 = a.
XOR everything.

questions.title: Number of 1 Bits
questions.summary: Count set bits of a positive integer.
hints: Look at bits one at a time, or smarter.
n & (n - 1) clears the lowest set bit.
Count how many times you can do that until n is 0.

questions.title: Counting Bits
questions.summary: Set-bit counts for every number 0..n in O(n).
hints: Reuse answers for smaller numbers.
i >> 1 has the same bits as i except the last.
bits[i] = bits[i >> 1] + (i & 1).

questions.title: Missing Number
questions.summary: The one number missing from 0..n.
hints: You know what the full range should sum to.
Expected sum - actual sum.
Or XOR all indices 0..n and all values.

questions.title: Reverse Bits
questions.summary: Reverse the 32 bits of an unsigned integer.
hints: Process one bit at a time.
Shift the result left, add n & 1, shift n right.
Repeat exactly 32 times (Java: >>> for unsigned shift).

questions.title: Longest Word in Dictionary
questions.summary: Longest word buildable one letter at a time from other words in the list.
hints: Every prefix must also be a word.
Trie with end flags.
DFS only through nodes that end a word; tie-break lexicographically.

questions.title: Sum of Two Integers
questions.summary: Add two integers without using + or −.
hints: XOR adds without carry.
AND then shift left gives the carry.
Repeat until carry is 0 (Python needs a 32-bit mask).

questions.title: Single Number II
questions.summary: Every element appears three times except one; find it in O(1) space.
hints: XOR alone cannot cancel triples.
Count each bit position across all numbers.
Bits whose count % 3 == 1 belong to the answer.

questions.title: Implement Magic Dictionary
questions.summary: Does a word match a dictionary word with exactly one character changed?
hints: Brute force over words of equal length works.
Or a trie DFS that allows exactly one mismatch.
Track whether the single change has been used.

questions.title: Maximum Product Subarray
questions.summary: Largest product of a contiguous subarray (values can be negative or zero).
hints: A negative number flips the largest into the smallest.
Track both the max and min product ending here.
At each x: new max/min come from x, max*x, min*x.

questions.title: Spiral Matrix
questions.summary: Return a matrix's elements in spiral order.
hints: Peel the outer layer, then repeat.
Keep top, bottom, left, right boundaries.
Move boundaries inward after each side; check they have not crossed.

questions.title: Set Matrix Zeroes
questions.summary: If a cell is 0, set its whole row and column to 0, in place.
hints: You need to remember which rows/columns to clear.
Use the first row and column as markers.
Track separately whether the first row/column themselves need clearing.

questions.title: Rotate Image
questions.summary: Rotate a square matrix 90° clockwise in place.
hints: Decompose the rotation into simpler steps.
Transpose the matrix.
Then reverse each row.

questions.title: Longest Palindromic Substring
questions.summary: Return the longest substring that reads the same both ways.
hints: Every palindrome has a center.
There are 2n - 1 centers (characters and gaps).
Expand around each center while the ends match.

questions.title: 3Sum Closest
questions.summary: Find three numbers whose sum is closest to a target.
hints: Same structure as 3Sum.
Sort, fix one number, two pointers for the rest.
Track the sum with the smallest absolute difference.

questions.title: Boats to Save People
questions.summary: Minimum boats when each boat carries at most two people within a weight limit.
hints: The heaviest person needs a boat now.
Sort; try pairing the heaviest with the lightest.
Two pointers: always move the heavy pointer, move light only if they fit together.

questions.title: Top K Frequent Words
questions.summary: The k most frequent words, ties broken alphabetically.
hints: Count words.
Order by (-count, word).
Heap of size k or full sort.

questions.title: Find K Pairs with Smallest Sums
questions.summary: k pairs (one from each sorted array) with the smallest sums.
hints: Do not generate all pairs.
Seed a min-heap with (nums1[i] + nums2[0]).
When popping (i, j), push (i, j + 1).

questions.title: Detonate the Maximum Bombs
questions.summary: Maximum bombs detonated by setting off one, with chain reactions.
hints: Bomb A reaches B is not symmetric. Directed graph.
Edge i→j if j is within i's radius (compare squared distances).
DFS/BFS from each bomb, take the max reach.

questions.title: Graph Valid Tree
questions.summary: Do the given edges form a valid tree on n nodes?
hints: A tree has exactly n - 1 edges.
And it must be connected / have no cycle.
Union-Find: fail on an edge joining nodes already connected.

questions.title: Jump Game III
questions.summary: From a start index, jump ± arr[i]; can you reach any zero?
hints: Indices are nodes with up to two edges.
BFS or DFS with visited.
Return true on reaching a 0.

questions.title: Find All Anagrams in a String
questions.summary: All start indices in s of substrings that are anagrams of p.
hints: Fixed window of length len(p).
Maintain letter counts for the window.
Record the start whenever the counts match p's counts.

questions.title: Candy
questions.summary: Minimum candies when higher-rated children must get more than their neighbours.
hints: Handle each direction separately.
Left pass: more than the left neighbour if rated higher.
Right pass: take the max with right-neighbour + 1.

questions.title: Non-decreasing Array
questions.summary: Can an array become non-decreasing by changing at most one element?
hints: Count violations nums[i] > nums[i+1].
More than one → false.
At a violation, lower nums[i] if possible, else raise nums[i+1].

questions.title: Minimum Number of Refueling Stops
questions.summary: Fewest refueling stops to reach a target with stations along the way.
hints: Delay the decision of where to refuel.
Push fuel of every station you pass into a max-heap.
When you run out, pop the largest fuel; fail if the heap is empty.

questions.title: Evaluate Division
questions.summary: Answer division queries from known equations like a / b = 2.
hints: Variables are nodes, ratios are weighted edges.
Add both a→b (k) and b→a (1/k).
DFS multiplying weights along the path; -1 if unreachable.

questions.title: Bitwise AND of Numbers Range
questions.summary: Bitwise AND of every number in a range.
hints: Any bit that changes inside the range becomes 0.
The answer is the common binary prefix of left and right.
Shift both right until equal, then shift back.

questions.title: Minimum Window Substring
questions.summary: Smallest window of s containing every character of t (with counts).
hints: Expand until the window contains everything, then shrink.
Track how many required characters are currently satisfied.
Shrink while still valid, recording the smallest window.

questions.title: Delete Node in a BST
questions.summary: Delete a value from a BST and keep it valid.
hints: Find the node first.
Zero or one child: replace with that child.
Two children: copy the in-order successor, then delete it from the right subtree.

questions.title: Convert Sorted Array to Binary Search Tree
questions.summary: Build a height-balanced BST from a sorted array.
hints: The root should split the array evenly.
Middle element as root.
Recurse on the left and right halves.
